newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee ends seesaw session mainly lower.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee ends seesaw session mainly lower.

text.p: A late-session sell-off by commission houses ahead of the weekend sent CSCE coffee prices mostly lower by the close on Friday, dealers said.

Spot May delivery fell 1.95 cents per lb on the day, to 189.10 cents, after trading from 194.80 to 187.50. Second-month July settled 1.60 cents lower, at 172.20 cents, while the back months closed down 2.10 to up 1.10.
Traders said much of the day's focus was on the May/July switch, which widened to near 20.00 cents during the session, but ended at 16.90, down from 17.25 cents at the close on Thursday.
Operators were gradually unwinding their May positions ahead of first notice day on April 22, they said. Open interest in May was down 755 lots Thursday, to 10,123 lots.
Prices seesawed between technical parameters throughout the day, traders said, with resistance at 195.00 cents and support at 187.00 cents basis May remaining intact.

On the fundamental side, a report by the Mexican Coffee Council showed the country's coffee exports totalled 651,495 60-kg bags in March, up 3.2 percent from the 631,513 bags sent abroad in the same month in 1996.
Analysts and traders said many Latin American countries have shipped heavily during the past two months to take advantage of the higher prices on the futures exchange.
They expect the increase in shipments to be reflected in the Green Coffee Association of New York's monthly stock data due after the close of business on April 15.

Stocks of green coffee stowed in U.S. warehouses are forecast to rise in March by 250,000 to 350,000 60-kg bags, most industry sources estimated. In February, GCA reported U.S. inventories increased by 204,000 bags, to 1,546,000 bags.
In March 1996, by comparison, U.S. consumer coffee stocks rose by 151,000 bags, to 2,372,000 bags, GCA data showed.

Prices on the CSCE tumbled last week on talk March GCA data would show a stock build of up to one million bags, but analysts said that while Latin American exports had been extremely heavy, not all the coffee turned up in the U.S.
"So much coffee went to Europe," said Merrill Lynch analysts Judith Ganes. "I don't see how it's possible to have a one million-bag increase."

Meanwhile, stocks certified against the exchange continued to inch lower. After Friday's close, CSCE reported certified coffee stocks were off 250 60-kg bags, to 81,078 bags as of April 10. There were no bags pending grading, the exchange said.
Traders await the latest CFTC Commitment of Traders report due late Friday. They said it is likely to show a decrease in non-commercial long positions.

While some traders said a decline in non-commercial long positions would be percieved as bullish since there would be room for the funds to get back into the market on the long side, others said the funds had taken their profits and may have left the market for the time being.
Volume reached an estimated 8,350 lots, down from Thursday's official tally of 10,903 lots.
